explanation: No single trigger. Strong activations land on very different tokens: prepositions after 'searches'/'until' in systematic-review methods sentences ('for', 'of', 'in'), mid-word pieces of names and foreign words ('eb', 'Z', 'aur', 'ic'), a year digit, 'ctl' in systemctl, and verbs in English, German, French and Japanese text. No token type or context predicts it reliably.

Mixed. It fires on the second word of fixed multi-word phrases ('See [also]', 'Appeal [from]', 'Massachusetts [Avenue]', 'Ice [Age]', 'Astronomical [Society]', 'lay[person]'), on the space before a year after a date, and on code and config tokens ('.h', 'offset', 'HKLM', '5' in a log pattern). These sets share no clear concept.

Fires on special symbols in scientific and technical text: Greek letters, either as Unicode (β, μ, κ, α) or as LaTeX names after a backslash (\alpha, \pi, \beta, \eta, \epsilon, \pm), plus the legal and copyright signs § and © and the ')' in 'Copyright (C)'. Math operators and brackets get moderate activation; ordinary words get almost none.

Fires on internal subword pieces of rare or foreign-looking words, typically the second or third token of a name or medical term ('urg' in Djurgården, 'CK' in Breckenridge or MDCK, 'cz' in Mieczysław or Eczema, 'ink' in rink, 'ani' in craniectomy, 'CG' in ECG). Whole common words get little or no activation.

Mixed. It fires on code-path and identifier tokens ('/assert', 'assertTrue', '.editor', '-equiv', '/licenses'), on German function words after prepositions ('dem', 'im', 'des'), and on the second part of proper names or multi-token terms ('McCain', 'Indies', 'Leone', 'ogeneity'). The groups do not share an evident concept.

Fires on the first subword fragment of a word split into pieces: an initial capital letter or letter pair of an abbreviation or gene/drug code ('D'PP, 'D'CM, 'R'aptiva, '-R'219K) or the first piece of a foreign or rare word ('ze', 'tr', 'ber', 'resc', 'al'). It also fires on the first byte of CJK characters in code comments, and occasionally on licence-boilerplate words.

Fires on tokens in formulaic or boilerplate phrases where the next word is highly predictable: math word problems ('highest common factor of', 'prime factors of'), legal citation boilerplate ('pro se', 'on the brief'), licence text ('in the hope that', 'name of copyright owner') and similar set phrases. The content varies widely, so the link between these groups is weak.

Fires on function words and comparatives inside quantifier, comparison or conditional constructions, where a complement must follow: 'more/less than', 'anything you need', 'any of these', 'no files to', 'greater than', 'not'. It is strongest in conditional or negated clauses such as 'if', 'any' or 'may not be in'.

Fires on separator or structural tokens that come right after a name or label and before a classification or value: the colon in taxonomic 'Diptera: Cecidomyiidae', 'family' in 'is a moth in the family X', the dot in version numbers ('2.0', '1.9'), and '=' or ';' in config and licence text. It also fires on some non-Latin script fragments. The pieces are loosely related.

Fires on color words, especially 'brown', also 'red', 'white', 'gray', 'yellow', 'black' and 'purple', when they describe the color of an object (wings, eyes, hair, fruit, pepper). It is strongest in descriptive or biological text; color names used as CSS values or tuple names give moderate activation.

Fires on the first token of a word or name that continues into further pieces, often a capital-letter onset of a transliterated name ('I' in Idukki or Ishaq, 'Abd', 'Ty') or a chemistry or medical prefix ('hyp', 'oh', 'ych', 'roph'). It also fires on the '.' in version numbers ('3.1', '2.0') and on commas between function arguments. The pieces are loosely related.

Fires on a letter suffix glued directly onto a number: unit or ordinal suffixes ('150cc', '21st', '20g', '44k', the 'Z' timestamp suffix) and letters inside alphanumeric codes or hex strings ('5883L', 'e204cc', '346e6429a'). A token gets near-zero activation when it is not attached to a preceding digit.

Mixed. It fires strongly on 'to' in licence boilerplate ('agreed to in writing'), 'license' and 'the' in copyright headers, and code identifiers or members ('Component', '.ID', '_middle'). It also fires on assorted words in prose ('bullied', 'age', '1' in 'Step 1'). Beyond the licence-header part there is no shared theme.

Fires on statistics and research-methods vocabulary in scientific abstracts: 'analyses', 'analysis', 'significance', 'hazard', 'cohort', 'systematic', 'descriptive', 'flow' cytometry, 'n'. It is strongest when the word names the analysis or study design in a methods or results sentence.
